docs.title: Recon AI Overview
docs.text: Welcome to the Recon AI User Guide. This platform allows you to automate the reconciliation of financial transactions, identifying discrepanices and validating data accuracy with powerful rule-based logic.

docs.title: Application Workflow
docs.text: The typical user journey in Recon AI follows a linear flow from data ingestion to analysis.

docs.title: 1. Data Connectors
docs.text:
Goal: Bring your data into the system.

  • Ingest: Upload files via CSV, Excel, JSON, connect to an SFTP Server, or integrate via API.
  • Map: Define how your file columns (e.g., Date, Amount, Reference) correspond to the system's schema.
  • See Data Connectors for more details.

docs.title: 2. Rules Engine
docs.text:
Goal: Define "what constitutes a match."

  • Create Rules: Use the logic builder to set conditions (e.g., Amount must match exactly, Date must be within 3 days).
  • Tolerances: Configure allowed variances for fuzzy matching.
  • See Rules Engine for more details.

docs.title: 3. Data Pipelines
docs.text:
Goal: Automate the processing.

  • Build Pipeline: Connect your Data Sources to your Rules.
  • Execution: Trigger pipelines manually to generate results.
  • See Data Pipelines for more details.

docs.title: 4. Reconciliation & Verification
docs.text:
Goal: Review results and handle exceptions.

  • Dashboard: Monitor the status of active jobs (Matched vs. Unmatched).
  • Manual Matching: Use the workspace to resolve exceptions that the automated rules could not handle.
  • See Reconciliation for more details.

docs.title: 5. Analytics
docs.text:
Goal: Visualize performance.

  • Executive Dashboard: View high-level KPIs, volume trends, and success rates.
  • See Analytics for more details.

docs.title: Roles & Permissions
docs.text: Recon AI uses a secure Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system.

docs.title: Admin Users
docs.text:
Administrators have full visibility and control over the platform.

  • System Settings: Configure global preferences.
  • User Management: Invite users and manage teams.
  • Audit Logs: View comprehensive system activity trails.

docs.title: Standard Users
docs.text:
Access for non-admin users is determined by their assigned Role.

  • Roles: Defined by Admins (e.g., Analyst, Reviewer).
  • Permissions: Granularity controls what actions a user can perform (e.g., View Only, Create & Edit, Delete).

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The Dashboard serves as the central hub of Recon AI, providing a real-time overview of your financial reconciliation status.

It is designed to give you immediate insights into key metrics, quick access to common tasks, and visibility into the system's operational health.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The page is organized into intuitive sections: - Header: Displays the page title and a brief description. - Quick Actions: A row of shortcuts for frequently performed tasks. - Key Metrics: A set of cards highlighting critical statistics like Total Volume, Success Rate, and Exception Rate. - Reconciliation Volume: A chart visualizing transaction trends over time. - System Health: A status monitor for system components.

docs.title: Quick Actions
docs.text:
The Quick Actions panel provides one-click access to essential functions:

  • Upload Data: Navigate to the data import interface to upload new transaction files.
  • Create Rule: Quickly define new matching logic or reconciliation rules.
  • Review Exceptions: Jump directly to the list of unmatched or flagged records requiring manual intervention.
  • View Analytics: Access detailed reports and analytical dashboards.
  • Manage Users: (Admin only) Add or modify user accounts and permissions.
  • System Settings: Configure global application settings.

docs.title: Key Metrics
docs.text:
This section displays vital performance indicators for the current period:

  • Total Volume:
    • Shows the total number of records processed (e.g., 1,395).
    • Includes a trend indicator (e.g., +100% from last month) to track growth.
  • Success Rate:
    • The percentage of records successfully matched automatically (e.g., 80.57%).
    • Displays the count of matched records against the total (e.g., 1,124 of 1,395 records matched).
    • A progress bar provides a visual representation of the completion rate.
  • Exception Rate:
    • The percentage of records that failed to match or triggered exceptions (e.g., 19.43%).
    • Indicates the number of items needing attention (e.g., 271 exceptions require review).
  • Processing Time:
    • The average time taken to process the batch (e.g., 17.5s).

docs.title: Reconciliation Volume
docs.text: A graph displaying the monthly transaction volume and matching results over a selected period (default: 6 Months). This helps in identifying trends in data influx and processing efficiency.

docs.title: System Health
docs.text:
A real-time monitor showing the status of system components.

  • Status: Displays Operational (Green) when systems are healthy.
  • Indicators: Provides visual confirmation that the backend services are running closely.

docs.title: User Activity Trends
docs.text:
A stacked bar chart visualizing weekly user activity, broken down by category:

  • Connectors (Green): Activities related to data connections.
  • Rules (Red): Creation or modification of reconciliation rules.
  • Pipelines (Yellow): Execution and management of data pipelines.

docs.title: Status Distribution
docs.text:
A donut chart providing an immediate visual breakdown of the current reconciliation status:

  • Auto-Matched (Green): Records successfully matched by the system.
  • Manual Match (Orange): Records matched manually by users.
  • Exceptions (Red): Unmatched records requiring attention.

docs.title: Recent Activity
docs.text: A log displaying the latest system events and user actions, helping administrators track changes and operations in real-time.

docs.title: Audit Log
docs.text: The Audit Log provides a comprehensive trail of all system activities and security events. It is an essential tool for monitoring compliance, investigating incidents, and tracking user actions.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The main interface displays a timeline of events alongside summary metrics.

docs.title: Summary Metrics
docs.text:
• Total Events: The total number of logged activities.
  • Errors: The count of failed operations or system errors.
  • Warnings: The number of non-critical alerts.
  • Unique Users: The count of distinct users who generated activity.

docs.title: Search and Filter
docs.text:
You can use the controls at the top to narrow down the log entries:

  • Search: Enter an email address to find logs related to a specific user.
  • Date Range: Select a Start Date and End Date to view events within a specific window.
  • Severity: Filter by All Severity, Info, Warning, or Error to focus on critical issues.

docs.title: Exporting Logs
docs.text:
Administrators can export audit logs for external analysis or archiving.

  1. Apply any desired filters (Date, Severity, etc.).
  2. Click the Export button.
  3. The system will generate a downloadable file containing the visible logs.

Constraint: You can export a maximum of 7 days of logs at a time. If you need data for a longer period, please perform multiple exports in 7-day chunks.

docs.title: Admin Dashboard
docs.text: The Admin Dashboard provides a centralized view for system administration and user management tasks. It is accessible only to users with administrative privileges.

docs.title: Overview Metrics
docs.text:
The top panel displays critical system statistics:

  • Total Users: The number of registered users in the organization.
  • Active Users: The count of users currently active.
  • Total Connectors: The number of configured data sources.
  • System Status: A real-time health indicator of the backend services.

docs.title: Quick Actions
docs.text:
Common administrative tasks are accessible via one-click buttons:

  • Invite User: Add new team members to the organization.
  • Manage Users: View and edit existing user accounts.
  • System Settings: Configure global parameters.
  • Audit Logs: Review system activity logs.

docs.title: Storage & Usage
docs.text:
Monitor the system's resource utilization to ensure optimal performance.

  • Storage Usage: A visual progress bar showing the amount of storage consumed against the allocated quota.
  • Occupied Storage: The exact amount of data currently stored (e.g., 47.86 MB).
  • Environment: Details about the current tenant or environment (e.g., test company).

docs.title: Roles & Permissions
docs.text: Recon AI employs a Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system, allowing administrators to define precise access levels for different users. The Roles & Permissions section is where you manage these definitions.

docs.title: Roles List
docs.text:
This view displays all available roles within your organization.

  • System Roles: Pre-defined roles (e.g., admin) that cannot be deleted but may have editable permissions.
  • Custom Roles: User-defined roles created to match specific organizational needs (e.g., analyst, viewer).
  • Summary: Quickly view the number of users assigned to a role and the count of enabled permissions.

docs.title: Creating & Editing Roles
docs.text:
You can create new roles or modify existing ones to tailor access rights.

  1. Click Create Role (or the Edit icon for an existing role).
  2. Define the role's identity and scope.

docs.title: Role Details
docs.text:
• Role Name: A unique name for the role.
  • Description: A brief explanation of the role's function.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Permissions are grouped by module (e.g., User Management, Connector Management).

  • Select Permissions: Check the boxes for specific actions you want to grant (e.g., Create User, View User, Update User, Delete User).
  • Grant Access: Once saved, users assigned this role will immediately inherit these permissions.

docs.title: System Settings
docs.text: The System Settings area allows administrators to configure global behavior and preferences for the Recon AI organization.

docs.title: General Settings
docs.text:
This section controls the fundamental properties of your tenant.

  • Organization Name: The display name of your entity (e.g., test company).
  • Timezone: The operational time zone used for logs, schedules, and reports (e.g., UTC-09:00).
  • Business Rules: The default logic set applied to reconciliation (e.g., Standard).
  • Default Currency: The primary currency for financial calculations (e.g., INR - Indian Rupee).

docs.title: Notification Settings
docs.text:
Manage how and when the system communicates with users.

You can toggle the following alerts on or off:

  • Email Notifications: Enable or disable all outbound emails.
  • System Alerts: Notifications regarding critical system errors or warnings.
  • Reconciliation Alerts: Updates on the status of reconciliation jobs (e.g., completion, failure).
  • Maintenance Notifications: Alerts about scheduled downtime or updates.

docs.title: User Management
docs.text: The User Management section allows administrators to control access to the Recon AI platform. You can invite new users, assign roles, and manage permissions.

docs.title: User List
docs.text:
The main view displays all users associated with your organization.

  • Search & Filter: Find users by name or status.
  • User Details: View Name, Email, Department, and assigned Roles.
  • Status: Indicates if a user is active or inactive.
  • Actions: Edit user details or remove them from the system.

docs.title: Inviting Users
docs.text:
To add a new member to your team, use the Invite User workflow.

  1. Click the Invite User button on the User Management page.
  2. You will be directed to the invitation form.

docs.title: Invitation Form
docs.text:
• Email Address: The recipient's email.
  • Full Name: The user's name.
  • Role: Assign a pre-defined role (e.g., Admin, Reviewer) to determine their permissions.
  • Department: (Optional) Specify the user's department.
  • Custom Message: Add a personal note to the invitation email.

Once you click Send Invitations, the user will receive an email with a link to join the organization. Upon acceptance and completion of their profile setup, they will be given access according to the assigned role.

docs.title: Executive Dashboard
docs.text: The Analytics Dashboard provides a comprehensive, high-level view of your reconciliation operations, allowing you to track performance, identify trends, and spot inefficiencies.

docs.title: Overview Metrics
docs.text:
The core KPIs at the top of the dashboard give you an instant pulse on your system's health.

  • Total Volume: The total number of transactions processed.
  • Success Rate: The percentage of records successfully matched.
  • Exception Rate: The percentage of records requiring manual intervention.
  • Processing Time: average time taken to process a batch or record.

docs.title: Period Comparison
docs.text:
Analyze your performance over time by comparing current metrics against historical data.

  • Timeframes: Switch between Week, Month, and Year views to see short-term fluctuations or long-term growth.
  • Trend Indicators: Visual cues (e.g., percentage changes) highlight whether metrics are improving or declining.

docs.title: Visual Trends and Distribution
docs.text:
Deep dive into the data with interactive charts.

  • Volume & Accuracy Trends: A dual-axis chart showing the correlation between transaction volume and match accuracy over the selected period.
  • Match Type Distribution: A stacked bar chart visualizing how records are being matched (e.g., One-to-One, One-to-Many) over time.

docs.title: Weekly Performance Trends
docs.text:
Track the detailed relationship between volume and accuracy on a weekly basis.

This line graph overlays Accuracy (green) and Volume (purple) to help correlations between high-load periods and matching efficiency.

docs.title: Performance Analysis
docs.text:
Understand the operational efficiency of your pipelines.

  • Reconciliation Processing Time: A line graph tracking the speed of your reconciliation jobs, helping you identify performance bottlenecks.
  • Reconciliation Status: A pie chart offering a breakdown of match categories (e.g., Exact, Tolerated Date, Manual Match).

docs.title: Job & Reconciliation Insights
docs.text:
Gain granular visibility into job performance and result composition.

  • Reconciliation Trends: A pie chart breaking down results into Matches, Mismatches, and Unmatched records.
  • Job Performance: A scatter plot correlating Volume vs. Accuracy, helping to identify outlying jobs that had high volume but low accuracy (or vice versa).

docs.title: Real-time Throughput
docs.text:
Monitor the engine's processing capabilities in real-time.

This multi-metric bar chart visualizes:

  • Job Count
  • Accuracy
  • Volume
  • Duration (Avg)
  • Result Counts (Matches, Mismatches, Unmatched)

docs.title: API Setup
docs.text: The API Setup page allows you to configure and manage direct integrations with external financial services and web applications.

docs.title: Managing Connections
docs.text:
• Add API Connection: Use the button to configure a new endpoint.
  • Status: Monitor the health and connectivity of your active integrations.

If no connections are configured, you will see a prompt to create your first API connection.

docs.title: File Upload
docs.text: The File Upload interface is the central location for managing all file-based data imports, including CSV, Excel, and JSON files.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This page displays a history of all uploaded files along with their processing status.

  • File Name: The name of the imported document.
  • Uploaded At: Timestamp of when the file was processed.
  • Source: The origin of the file (e.g., User upload).
  • File Type: The format of the data (csv, json, etc.).
  • Mapping Status: Indicates if the file columns have been mapped to the system schema (e.g., Mapped).

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Users can perform specific actions on each record:

  • Edit: Modify mapping or file details.
  • Download: Retrieve the original file.
  • Delete: Remove the file from the system (if permitted).

You can also initiate new uploads using the buttons at the top right:

docs.title: Upload File
docs.text: Clicking Upload File opens the local upload interface. Here, you can drag and drop your file or browse your system to select a CSV, Excel, or JSON file for immediate processing.

docs.title: Upload from SFTP
docs.text: Clicking Upload from SFTP redirects you to the server selection page. You must first choose a configured SFTP server to browse and select files residing on the remote system.

docs.title: Browsing Files
docs.text:
Once you select a connector, you will be taken to the Browse SFTP Files interface.

  • Navigate: Click on folders to explore the directory structure of the remote server.
  • Select: Choose the specific file you wish to import.
  • Map: After selecting a file, you can proceed to the mapping stage to define how the file's columns relate to your schema.

docs.title: Data Connectors Hub
docs.text: The Data Connectors Hub is your starting point for importing transaction data into Recon AI. It supports various methods to ensure flexible integration with your existing financial systems.

docs.title: Available Connectors
docs.text:
• CSV Upload: Import comma-separated value files manually.
  • Excel Upload: Support for .xlsx spreadsheet formats.
  • JSON Upload: Import structured JSON data files.
  • API Connection: Set up direct integration with external services for real-time data pulling.
  • SFTP Server: Configure secure file transfer protocol connections for automated batch processing.

Note: Selecting CSV Upload, Excel Upload, or JSON Upload will direct you to the unified File Upload interface to manage your files.

docs.title: SFTP Server
docs.text: The SFTP Server section allows you to manage secure file transfer connections for automated data retrieval. This is ideal for batch processing large volumes of transaction data on a scheduled basis.

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
Each configured connection displays key information:

  • Host/Address: The address of the SFTP server (e.g., 0.tcp.in.ngrok.io).
  • Port: The connection port (e.g., 14428).
  • Remote Path: The directory on the server where files are located.
  • Status: Last sync time and connection health.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Test: Verify connectivity with the server.
  • Edit: specific configuration details.
  • Delete: Remove the connection configuration.

docs.title: Creating a Pipeline
docs.text: Building a data pipeline involves configuring the basic parameters and then visually designing the data flow.

docs.title: Basic Information
docs.text:
Set the identity and schedule for the pipeline.

  • Pipeline Name: A descriptive name for the workflow.
  • Processing Schedule: Define when the pipeline runs (e.g., Manual or scheduled frequency).

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text:
Define the inputs and outputs for your data.

  • Source Data Connectors: Select where data comes from (e.g., specific files or API endpoints).
  • Target Data Connectors: Select where processed data should be sent (optional).

docs.title: Step 2: Workflow Canvas
docs.text: After configuration, you enter the Interactive Pipeline Canvas, where you define the logic flow.

docs.title: Building the Workflow
docs.text:
1. Node Palette: On the right, you have access to available components (Source Connectors, Rules, Target Connectors).
  2. Drag and Drop: Pull nodes onto the canvas to represent steps in your process.
  3. Connect Nodes: Draw lines between the ports of different nodes to define the data path.
    • Connect Source Data -> Rule Components for reconciliation.
    • Connect Rule Components -> Target Data (if applicable).
  4. Run Test: Verify the logic before activating.

docs.title: Data Pipeline Management
docs.text: Data Pipelines automate the flow of information between your connectors and the reconciliation engine. This dashboard provides a centralized view of all processing workflows.

docs.title: Dashboard Metrics
docs.text:
• Total Pipelines: The number of configured workflows.
  • Active Pipelines: The number of workflows currently enabled.
  • Avg Success Rate: The historical reliability of your data processing.
  • Records Processed: The volume of data handled by the pipelines.

docs.title: Managing Pipelines
docs.text:
The list view allows you to control each pipeline:

  • Run Pipeline: Manually trigger an immediate execution.
  • Edit/Pause/Delete: Manage the configuration and state of the workflow.
  • History: View logs of previous executions.

docs.title: Reconciliation Management
docs.text: The Reconciliation Dashboard is where you monitor the execution and results of your matching processes.

docs.title: Overview Metrics
docs.text:
Top-level statistics provide an immediate health check of your operations:

  • Active Jobs: The number of reconciliation processes currently running or pending.
  • Records Matched: The total volume of successful matches found.
  • Exceptions: The number of records that failed to match and require manual attention.
  • Success Rate: The percentage of automated matches against total volume.

docs.title: Reconciliation Jobs
docs.text:
This list displays individual job executions with detailed results:

  • Status: E.g., COMPLETED, RUNNING.
  • Pipeline: The specific pipeline that generated the job.
  • Matched/Unmatched: Quick counts of the results.
  • Accuracy: The efficiency score of the specific run.
  • Action: Click View Details to dive deeper into specific jobs.

docs.title: Matching Workspace
docs.text: The Matching Workspace is an interactive environment for resolving exceptions and fine-tuning your data reconciliation. It allows human review of complex cases that the automated rules could not resolve with certainty.

docs.title: Manual Matching
docs.text: The Manual Matching interface gives you full control over the reconciliation of specific records.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Filter: Use the controls at the top to select specific pipelines, exception types, or match categories.
  2. Review: Examine the Source Record and Target Record side-by-side.
    • Unmatched: The system found no suitable candidate.
    • Partial: A potential match was found but fell outside strictly defined tolerances.
  3. Action:
    • Find and Match: Search for the correct counterparty record manually.
    • Approve/Reject: For partial matches, validate if the system's suggestion is correct.

docs.title: Match Suggestions
docs.text: (Under Development) This section presents AI-driven proposals for matches, allowing users to bulk-approve high-probability pairings to speed up the review process.

docs.title: Rules Engine Overview
docs.text: The Rules Engine is the core intelligence of Recon AI, allowing you to define, manage, and monitor the logic used for automated data reconciliation.

docs.title: Dashboard Metrics
docs.text:
The top overview panel provides a snapshot of your rule performance:

  • Total Rules: The count of all rules defined in the system.
  • Active Rules: The number of rules currently enabled and processing data.
  • Avg Accuracy: The overall efficiency and precision of your matching logic.
  • Records Matched: The total number of successful matches generated by the engine.

docs.title: Managing Rules
docs.text:
The Reconciliation Rules list allows you to control individual rules:

  • Status Indicators: Quickly see if a rule is active, its validation level (e.g., Rule-Based), and its priority (High, Medium, Low).
  • Actions:
    • Pause/Resume: Toggle the rule's activity status.
    • Edit: Modify the rule's logic or configuration.
    • Delete: Remove the rule from the system.

docs.title: Rule Builder
docs.text: The Rule Builder provides a visual interface for constructing complex reconciliation logic without writing code.

docs.title: Step 1: Rule Information
docs.text:
First, define the metadata and scope of your rule.

  • Rule Name: unique identifier for the rule (min 2 chars).
  • Description: A detailed explanation of the rule's purpose (min 10 chars).
  • Priority: Set the execution precedence (Medium default).
  • Timeline Filter: Restrict the data scope (e.g., Past 30 Days).
  • Status: Set the initial state of the rule (Active or Inactive).

docs.title: Step 2: Logic Builder
docs.text: After saving the basic info, you proceed to the drag-and-drop conditions builder.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• Match Types: Define the strategy (e.g., One-to-One, One-to-Many).
  • Tolerances: Allow for minor variances in Date or Amount to improve match rates.
  • Match Criteria: Configure specific field-level matching logic.
  • Conditions: Set logical constraints.

To build a rule, simply drag a component from the left panel into the Conditions Builder canvas on the right.
